transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I keep checking things. Folders, drawers, little labeled boxes where I keep papers and keepsakes. I’ll look to make sure they’re still there, and then a few minutes later I’m back checking again. It’s taking up too much of the day.
When you check your folders, drawers, or boxes, do you have upsetting thoughts or images that come to mind, like a fear that something bad will happen if they’re not in order?

Yes… not exactly that something awful will happen, but I get this thought that I might have thrown away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. I know it probably isn’t true, but it keeps needling at me, and then I feel like I’ve been terribly careless unless I check.

When you get these thoughts about possibly misplacing things, does checking them give you a sense of relief, or are you mainly trying to prevent something bad from happening, even if it’s not exactly clear what that something is?

I suppose it’s more relief than anything. I open the same folders and drawers, the labeled boxes… just to see the papers or keepsakes are still where I left them. Even if I only checked a few minutes before, I feel pushed to look again.
Can you describe what goes through your mind just before you feel the need to check the folders or boxes again? Is it a specific thought, a feeling, or something else that makes you want to check?

It’s usually just a thought that won’t leave me alone. I’ll think, well, maybe I threw away my husband’s old tax papers, or maybe I put a family recipe in the wrong box. I know, really, that it’s probably not so… but it keeps at me, and then I feel as if I’ve been terribly careless unless I look.
Do these thoughts about possibly misplacing items feel intrusive and unwanted, like they come into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yes… they do feel unwanted. Even when I know better, the thought keeps needling me that I may have thrown away my husband’s tax papers or put a recipe in the wrong box. I can’t quite let it pass without feeling I’ve been terribly careless.
Do these thoughts and the need to check your folders and boxes interfere with other parts of your day, like work, social activities, or time with family?

Yes… it does, more than I like to admit. I’ve had to cancel my mentoring sometimes, and I’ve missed book club because I lose whole afternoons going through things. Then I’m too embarrassed to have anyone over, with the apartment still such a mess.
When you have these thoughts about possibly misplacing things, do you feel driven to check them to reduce your anxiety, or is it more to make sure everything is just right or in its proper place?

More to quiet myself, I suppose. I keep opening the same folders or drawers, the labeled boxes… just to be sure the papers and keepsakes are still where I left them. Even if I looked only a few minutes before, I feel pushed to check again.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you a lot of distress, even when you’re not in the middle of checking?

Yes… it does bother me. Even when I’m not actually looking through things, the thought can sit there, like maybe I threw out my husband’s old tax papers or put a recipe where it doesn’t belong. I know it may not make sense, but I still feel as if I’ve been terribly careless.

Do you ever feel that certain numbers, arrangements, or patterns are important for things to feel right, or do your checking behaviors mostly revolve around fears of having misplaced something important?

No, not so much numbers or patterns. It’s mostly that nagging thought that I’ve put something important in the wrong place… or worse, thrown it away. Even when I know I probably haven’t, it keeps at me. Like my husband’s old tax papers, or a family recipe in the wrong box. I feel… careless, I suppose, if I don’t check.
